note: THE HALL -- the Kingdom tab's CHAT sub-tab (scenes/kingdom/chat_section.gd). The painting's own header and its two tab rows are NOT cut: the Kingdom tab keeps kingdom.png's header, and both rows are TabStrips built from tabs_sheet.json's short plates, as every strip of three or more is. What is cut here is what the hall itself is made of -- the day's rule, a lord's plates and bubble, the realm's horn and scroll, and the bar a line is written on. A round portrait is portraits/avatar_<id>_ring with the lord's own frame over it (Look.paint_frame), the same object the Kingdom's medallions and the rankings' podium draw, so a lord looks the same in the hall as everywhere else.

crops.name: chat/divider_left
crops.note: The day's rule, left half, ending in the painting's diamond. The word between the two halves is live (TODAY, YESTERDAY, a date), so it is set in type between them rather than erased out of one long rule -- an erase across a gold rule leaves a flat bar where the light was.

crops.name: chat/divider_right
crops.note: The same rule's right half, starting at its own diamond.

crops.name: chat/crown
crops.note: The crown over a king's or a marshal's name. A member's line has none, which is how the painting marks rank in the hall.

crops.name: chat/name_plate
crops.note: The gold-rimmed plate a lord's name is set on. Empty as painted.

crops.name: chat/time_plate
crops.note: The steel-rimmed plate beside it, for when the line was said.

crops.name: chat/bubble
crops.note: What a lord said: the navy bubble with its tail on the left, toward the portrait. Nine-patched, so a long line grows the bubble and not the tail -- the left margin has to clear the tail (x 316-325) or a stretched bubble drags the point across the page.

crops.name: chat/horn
crops.note: The herald's horn and banner, drawn beside the FIRST line of a run the realm says. The painting shows it on the first and third system lines and not on the second, which is exactly what a run looks like.

crops.name: chat/scroll
crops.note: The parchment a system line is written on: a lord joined, gold was given, a Work rose, the treasury was opened. Nine-patched.

crops.name: chat/bar
crops.note: The bar a line is written on, with the quill and its parchment field baked in: it is one object at one size (the page's own width), so nothing here is nine-patched and nothing is stretched. SEND is lifted off it row by row from the bar's own navy just left of the plate (x 736-748) and cut separately, because a plate that dims when the hall is shut has to be a button and not a painted patch.

crops.name: chat/send
crops.note: SEND, the word baked: it never changes. Dimmed while the hall is shut or the line is empty.
